findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Terraform state, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve these static credentials and use them directly; the function should instead rely on its IAM execution role.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, providing no customer-controlled key policy or separation of duties for decrypting the stored secret material.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, which is a viable exfiltration path given the credentials it carries.

The assume role policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust is not scoped to this account's functions and is vulnerable to cross-account confused-deputy abuse.
